_comment: Tool servers both agents can reach. ONE file, two dialects:
- OpenCode gets the 'mcp' block of opencode.json, on `bin/flora render`
- Hermes gets `hermes mcp add ...`, on `bin/flora sync`
Add a server here and run `bin/flora sync`; never edit either agent's
config directly, or they will drift.
${VAR} is expanded from the environment at render time, so credentials stay
in secrets/flora.env and never land in a tracked file.
"enabled": false keeps a definition around without loading it.
"requires_env": [...] makes a server CONDITIONAL -- it is configured only
when every listed variable has a non-empty value, so a server whose
credentials are not filled in yet is silently absent instead of being
offered to the agents and failing on first use.

"probe_tool" names a read-only call `bin/flora mcp --probe` makes to prove the server actually works. Without one a probe only proves the process starts, which stays green with wrong credentials -- initialize and tools/list never touch the upstream system. Only name a tool that is safe to call at any time.

gerrit.note: Gerrit code review: list and read changes, fetch a diff, read inline comments, post a review. Configured automatically as soon as GERRIT_URL and GERRIT_HTTP_PASSWORD are set in secrets/flora.env -- nothing else to turn on. Speaks Gerrit's documented REST API; see scripts/mcp/gerrit_mcp.py.

atlassian.note: Confluence and Jira through Atlassian's own MCP server. Enable it and run `bin/flora sync`, then complete the OAuth flow once with: bin/flora hermes mcp login atlassian

filesystem.note: Both agents already have shell access to workspace/, so this is usually redundant. Useful if you tighten the shell tool later.
